name: Spoils
overview: The Scriptures reveal that spoils, or goods taken in war, were a tangible result of Israel's military victories, as seen when Abram's allies took the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and rescued Lot (Genesis 14:11-12). In later accounts, such as the conflict with Midian, Israel took spoils including livestock, goods, and captives, while also destroying enemy cities (Numbers 31:9-10). The distribution of these spoils was carefully regulated by the Lord through Moses, involving priests and leaders in the process to ensure proper handling and dedication to God (Numbers 31:25-26). This demonstrates the biblical principle that war spoils were not merely personal gain but were subject to divine oversight and consecration.
